name: LM311DT
title: LM111, LM211, LM311: voltage comparator with strobe
summary: A single voltage comparator with low input currents, working from one +5 V logic supply up to ±15 V. The output is an uncommitted transistor: its collector can switch loads up to 50 V (40 V for LM311) at up to 50 mA, and its emitter can be grounded or used as an emitter-follower output, suiting RTL, DTL, TTL and MOS logic. Strobe and offset-balance pins are provided. LM111, LM211 and LM311 differ in temperature range and limits; LM311DT is the 0 °C to +70 °C grade in SO-8.

circuits.title: Crystal oscillator
circuits.description: A 100 kHz crystal oscillator on a single +5 V supply. R1 and R2, equal, divide the supply onto the non-inverting input; the crystal in series with C2 feeds the output back to that input. R3 from the output and C1 to ground form the inverting input. R4 pulls the output up.

circuits.title: Low voltage adjustable reference supply
circuits.description: An adjustable low-voltage reference running from +5 V. Q1 (2N1304) with its base tied to its collector, stacked on Q2 (2N2222) whose base shares that node, is fed through R1 and sets the voltage on the non-inverting input. The output, pulled up by R4, drives a divider of rheostat R3 and R2 into the inverting input, so R3 sets the output level. C1, a solid tantalum part, sits across the output.

circuits.title: 100 kHz free running multivibrator
circuits.description: A 100 kHz square-wave oscillator on +5 V. R1 and R2 divide the supply onto the non-inverting input and R4 feeds the output back to it. R3 from the output and C1 to ground form the inverting input, so C1 charges and discharges as the output switches. R5 pulls the output up.
notes: The output drives a TTL or DTL fan-out of two.

circuits.title: TTL interface with high level logic
circuits.description: Brings a 0 to 30 V logic signal down to TTL. R1 and R2 divide the input onto the non-inverting input, with C1 across R2; R3 and R4 split the +5 V supply onto the inverting input as the reference, which places the switching point at 15 V on the input. R5 pulls the output up to +5 V for the TTL load.
notes: Input swing 0 to 30 V, threshold 15 V.

circuits.title: Strobe
circuits.description: Driving the strobe from TTL: the collector of an NPN transistor goes to STROBE/BALANCE, its emitter to ground through 1 kΩ, and its base to the TTL strobe line.
notes: A fragment: U1's supply, ground and BALANCE pins are not part of it.

circuits.title: Increasing input stage current
circuits.description: BALANCE, STROBE/BALANCE and VCC+ tied together to the positive supply raise the current in the input stage; the Raised curves of input offset and bias current against temperature are for this connection.
notes: A fragment: U1's VCC- and GND pins are not part of it.

circuits.title: Offset balancing
circuits.description: Offset null: a 5 kΩ potentiometer runs between BALANCE and STROBE/BALANCE, and its wiper goes through 3 kΩ to VCC+.
notes: A fragment: U1's VCC- and GND pins are not part of it.

equations.name: Equivalent input offset voltage
equations.note: Plotted against RS for LM111/LM211 and for LM311.

operation.text: Runs from split ±15 V supplies down to a single +5 V supply. The offset and bias limits hold over that whole span. Total supply is rated to 36 V.

The output is an NPN transistor with its collector on OUTPUT and its emitter reaching GND through 4 Ω. With GND at ground and a pull-up on OUTPUT it works as an open-collector output; the collector may sit up to 50 V (LM111, LM211) or 40 V (LM311) above VCC-. With OUTPUT at VCC+ and a load from GND, the output follows as an emitter follower.

Output current is 50 mA, with VOL 0.75 V typical at that current. Short-circuit current peaks near 120 mA at about 2 V on the output and falls to about 40 mA at 15 V, where dissipation reaches about 0.65 W. Output short circuit is rated for 10 s.
STROBE/BALANCE is driven by an NPN transistor (2N2222, 1 kΩ in the emitter) switched by a TTL strobe signal. Strobe current is 3 mA typical.
A 5 kΩ potentiometer across BALANCE and STROBE/BALANCE, with its wiper taken to VCC+ through 3 kΩ, nulls the input offset.
Tying BALANCE and STROBE/BALANCE to VCC+ raises the input stage current. At 25 °C input bias current goes from about 70 nA to about 280 nA, and offset current from about 4 nA to about 10 nA.
Input bias current steps with differential input: about 150 nA below -6 V, about 93 nA from -6 V to 0 V and about 60 nA from 0 V to +6 V, at ±15 V and 25 °C.
Over 0 °C to 70 °C the inputs work to within about 1.0 V to 1.1 V of VCC+ and about 0.2 V to 0.3 V of VCC-.
